solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Step on it! AI out of control in plant!

indicators.note: letters that are out of control run wild and end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An urgent shout to hurry because an artificial intelligence has gone rogue inside a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step on it!' reads as a command to hurry, but it is just letters to be mixed with AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican shrub with red bracts, sold as a Christmas pot plant.

clue.text: Survey of Italian river and Lakes

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
L is short for lake; doubling it makes the plural, as pp does for pages

explanation.surface: A study of an Italian river together with some lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A poll is a survey of opinion, a canvassing of people's views.

clue.text: Home and dry, welcoming wanderer, not a good mixer

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the teetotal pair of letters takes the wanderer in between them, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who does not drink
a rover is someone who roams

explanation.surface: Someone at home and sober who takes in a traveller, yet is not sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' means abstaining from alcohol, so it gives TT (teetotal).
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a shy, inward-looking person who is uneasy in company.

clue.text: Uninhibited activity in German river

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bout of unrestrained indulgence
second meaning: the river that flows through Berlin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests wild behaviour on a German river; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a lively bout of indulgence, and the Spree is also the river running through Berlin.

clue.text: Having sixth sense leaving home to get some education

indicators.note: the word for home departs from the longer word, so its letters are dropped

parts.note: intuition is the instinctive knowing sometimes called a sixth sense
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A person with a sixth sense leaves home in order to be educated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, a portion of someone's schooling.

clue.text: In land strip's first hotel, meeting male, American

parts.note: 1st, written with the numeral read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Arriving at the first hotel on a narrow strip of land, someone meets an American man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' gives IST, the abbreviation 1st with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow neck of land joining two larger landmasses, such as Panama.

clue.text: Back in Slavonian sports ground

indicators.note: the letters picked out are read backwards
the answer sits inside the word Slavonian

parts.note: the hidden letters are the second to fifth of this word

explanation.surface: Back in Slavonia, someone looks for a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, though any oval-shaped field counts.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is a ground for sport, especially cricket or Australian football.

clue.text: Worth showing lack of precision after change of heart

indicators.note: the letter at the centre of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: something vague is imprecise or unclear

explanation.surface: Worth has lost precision since someone changed their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the five-letter word is its middle letter, G, which becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Value is what something is worth, its merit or price.

clue.text: Belief Braille needs tweaking is mystery initially

indicators.note: tweaking means adjusting, so the letters of the first word are rearranged
initially takes the first letter of the word mystery

explanation.surface: A view that the Braille system needs adjusting is a puzzle at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange BRAILLE to LIBERAL, then add IS and M, the first letter of mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberalism is a political creed favouring individual freedom and tolerance.

clue.text: Son working with mower, up-to-the- minute, here

definitions.note: a description of the place where the latest stories are handled, not a synonym for the answer

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son operating a lawn mower, with the latest news delivered here.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the place where up-to-the-minute matters are dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsroom is the office where journalists gather and edit current stories.

clue.text: Afterwards, state of agitation as husband leaves

indicators.note: the husband departs from the word, so his letter is dropped

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be worked up and flustered

explanation.surface: After the husband walks out, someone is left in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, coming after the present.

clue.text: Expecting favourite, that specific one in suit

parts.note: something in is fashionable or in favour
the definite article points to one particular thing
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Expecting a favourite to turn up in one particular suit.
explanation.walkthrough: In the club is informal British slang for pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom in the club means pregnant, so it matches expecting a baby.

clue.text: No Blue, I'm for reform — it's elementary

definitions.note: a playful description: the answer is a chemical element, not a synonym

indicators.note: the letters are up for reshaping into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are no longer a Tory blue and wants reform, calling it simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is the colour of the Conservatives; 'elementary' is a pun on element.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobelium is a synthetic radioactive chemical element, number 102, named after Alfred Nobel.

clue.text: Guidance in haste, erratic

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the answer straddles the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Advice given in a hurried, unpredictable way.
explanation.definitionFit: Steer is informal for advice or direction, as in a useful steer.

clue.text: Snag at toll resolved — not before time!

indicators.note: the letters are broken down and rearranged, as a problem is resolved

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hold-up at a toll booth is finally sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as the snag being settled, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: At long last expresses relief that something has happened after a lengthy wait.

clue.text: After time, think logically: 'It's a crime'

indicators.note: the reasoning word follows the time letter

parts.note: to reason is to think things through logically

explanation.surface: After a pause, someone thinks it through and declares an act criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign.

clue.text: Slow-moving one, female, is in Paris for boxing match

parts.note: a slug is a byword for sluggishness
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A slow creature and a woman are in Paris for a prize fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is informal for a fight or bout with heavy punches traded.

clue.text: Not complaining lots about taking vicar in — away from borders

indicators.note: with in, the outer letters take the core of vicar inside them
completes the instruction to place one piece within the other
the word lots is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outside letters of vicar are removed, leaving its middle

parts.note: only its inner letters are used

explanation.surface: Someone uncomplaining despite much fuss about taking in a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoical person bears hardship patiently without grumbling.

clue.text: Angry about current worker roll

indicators.note: the angry word goes around the symbol for current

parts.note: cross means annoyed
I is the physics symbol for electric current
the worker ant is the crossword stock worker

explanation.surface: Someone angry about the present state of a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' is the bread sense, not a movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped bread roll made of flaky pastry.

clue.text: Push one's views on others in redoubt — out of order!

indicators.note: the letters are disordered and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone imposes opinions in a fortification and is told off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A redoubt is a small fort; 'out of order' doubles as the scolding phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to impose oneself or one's ideas on people unasked.

clue.text: Come next, carrying exactly what's needed for describing some bathrooms

indicators.note: the word for following holds the other piece within it

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on
it, as in 'that's it', means the very thing required

explanation.surface: Something follows on, bringing just the right touch for a bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite bathroom is one attached directly to a bedroom.

clue.text: Try to accommodate Monsieur with musical work missing page, lofty in style

indicators.note: the trying word houses the abbreviation for Monsieur

parts.note: to have a pop is to have a try
M is the French abbreviation, as in M. Poirot

indicators.note: the page letter is absent from the composition

parts.note: an opus is a numbered composition

explanation.surface: An attempt to fit a French gentleman into a musical piece that has lost a page, in a grand manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous means self-important and grandiloquent, affecting a superior manner.

clue.text: Friend bringing in artist's old sunshade

indicators.note: the friend word takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a pal is a mate
RA, Royal Academician, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A friend fetches an artist's old sunshade.
explanation.walkthrough: An RA is a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, so artist's gives RAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella carried to keep off the sun.

clue.text: Fellow for example coming back and not working

indicators.note: the abbreviation for example is read in reverse

parts.note: a machine that is off is not running

explanation.surface: A man, for instance, coming back and idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoff is a man's name, and a fellow is any man.

clue.text: Gas region with nothing earlier

indicators.note: the nothing letter comes before the region word

parts.note: O looks like zero
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: A gas once filled an empty region.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a pungent form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule.

clue.text: Knight is curious, we hear — that's a turn- up

indicators.note: the pieces are spoken and give a word of the same sound

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title, and to pry is to be inquisitive, so a knight is curious is Sir pries

explanation.surface: A nosy knight, it is said, produces an unexpected event.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn-up, short for turn-up for the books, is British for an unexpected outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise is an unexpected event, which is exactly a turn-up.

clue.text: Hood maybe as formal dressing? Not quite

indicators.note: the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: robing is putting on ceremonial robes

explanation.surface: A hood worn as part of formal academic dress, not quite complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like the garment but is Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is the first name of Hood, the legendary Sherwood outlaw.

clue.text: Time unchanged after reflection

indicators.note: the word reads the same when mirrored, backwards as forwards

parts.note: midday, read both as definition and as the word that is mirrored

explanation.surface: A time that stays the same when seen in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, twelve o'clock, a fixed point of time.

clue.text: So caustic about quality of sound

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cutting remark about how a hall sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustics are the properties of a room that determine how sound carries in it.

clue.text: Well done! Charlie will come next

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shout of approval
second meaning: the NATO phonetic code word immediately before Charlie

explanation.walkthrough: In the phonetic alphabet Alpha, Bravo, Charlie stand for A, B, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is a cheer of applause and also the radio code word for B, preceding Charlie.

clue.text: Cup match followed by right row

parts.note: a tie is a knockout match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: A cup fixture is followed by an argument over rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line or level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, such as one of several rising rows of seats.

clue.text: Prime Minister once favourably placed, winning in end, not for turning

parts.note: to be well placed is to be in a good position
taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of winning is used

parts.note: its last letter is taken

indicators.note: the word not is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former premier, well placed and winning in the end, refuses to change course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not for turning' recalls Thatcher's line, but another PM is meant: the Duke of Wellington.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo, served as British Prime Minister in 1828-30.
